events.label: birth
events.text: Schembri was born; later a Maltese forward.

evidence.quote: born 27 May 1986

events.text: Made first-team debut with Hibernians in the 2002–03 season.

evidence.quote: Schembri started out as a trainee with Hibernians making his first team debut in the 2002–03 season

events.text: Played first UEFA competition match, youth international vs Armenia.

evidence.quote: His first game in a UEFA competition was on 5 March 2002 against Armenia

events.text: Made European competition debut with Hibernians in Intertoto Cup.

evidence.quote: He made his debut in a European competition on 19 June 2004

events.text: Joined Marsaxlokk after transfer from Hibernians.

evidence.quote: Schembri joined the club on 29 January 2005

events.label: title
events.text: Marsaxlokk won first league title, Schembri a key forward.

evidence.quote: leading the latter to their first league title in the 2006–07 season

events.text: Made senior Malta national team debut vs Japan.

evidence.quote: making his senior debut on 4 June 2006 against Japan
On 4 June 2006 , Schembri made his debut with the Maltese national team

events.label: international_goal
events.text: Scored first two international goals in 2–1 win over Hungary.

evidence.quote: played at Ta Qalis National Stadium on 11 October 2006
His first goals came in the historic 2–1 win over Hungary

events.text: Joined Eintracht Braunschweig on season-long loan.

evidence.quote: In the summer of 2007 , with interest from foreign clubs including OFI Crete , Schembri joined Eintracht Braunschweig

events.text: Joined Carl Zeiss Jena on another loan.

evidence.quote: as in June 2008 he joined 3 . Liga side Carl Zeiss Jena on another loan

events.text: Joined Austria Kärnten on a two-year deal.

evidence.quote: Schembri joined Austria Kärnten on a two-year deal on 19 June 2009

events.label: award
events.text: Named Malta's Sportsman of the Year.

evidence.quote: Maltas Sportsman of the Year : 2010

events.text: Released from Austria Kärnten contract.

evidence.quote: Schembri was one of few players who was allowed to be released in January 2010

events.text: Signed with Ferencváros, became key forward.

evidence.quote: Ferencváros signed Schembri in February 2010

events.text: Joined Olympiacos Volou.

evidence.quote: he joined Olympiacos Volou on 7 July 2011

events.text: Joined Panionios on one-year contract after Olympiacos rescission.

evidence.quote: signing a one-year contract on 30 September 2011

events.text: Signed two-year deal with Omonia.

evidence.quote: On 20 August 2012 , Cypriot club Omonia signed Schembri on a two-year deal

events.text: Joined FSV Frankfurt in 2. Bundesliga; lasted six months.

evidence.quote: During the summer of 2014 , with the chance of joining a higher-level league , Schembri joined 2 . Bundesliga side FSV Frankfurt

events.text: Rescinded contract with FSV Frankfurt.

evidence.quote: he returned to Omonia in December 2014
Schembri rescinded his contract in December

events.text: Returned to Omonia on 18-month contract.

evidence.quote: he returned to Omonia in December 2014
In the same month he agreed to re-join Omonia on an 18-month contract

events.text: Captained Malta national team for the first time.

evidence.quote: Schembri captained Malta for the first time on 25 March 2015

events.text: Married Clarissa Ellul at St. Paul's Church, Rabat.

evidence.quote: He married Clarissa Ellul , a television presenter , on 3 June 2016

events.text: Boavista officially announced his transfer.

evidence.quote: on 16 June 2016 , Primeira Liga club Boavista officially announced Schembris transfer

events.text: Removed as Malta captain, replaced by Michael Mifsud.

evidence.quote: For the following match against Lithuania on 11 October , Schembri was removed as captain

events.label: charity_support
events.text: Began supporting Dr. Klown clown-doctor NGO with Apollon.

evidence.quote: Since 2017 , Schembri and Apollon Limassol have been supporting Dr . Klown

events.text: Signed with Apollon Limassol, returning to Cyprus.

evidence.quote: On 13 June 2017 , Schembri signed with Apollon Limassol

events.label: trophy
events.text: Won Cypriot Super Cup with Apollon; first trophy abroad.

evidence.quote: In August 2017 , he won his first trophy outside his home country

events.label: first_uefa_goal
events.text: Equaliser vs Atalanta; first Maltese to score in UEFA proper rounds.

evidence.quote: against Atalanta played on 19 October , Schembri scored the temporary equaliser

events.text: Published autobiographical book, 10 years playing in Europe.

evidence.quote: In June 2018 , he published an autobiographical book

events.text: Retirement from national team, stated as October 2018.

evidence.quote: at the time of his retirement in October 2018

events.text: Announced retirement from international football after Nations League.

evidence.quote: On 13 November 2018 , Schembri announced that he would be retiring from international football

events.text: Last Malta international match, 1–1 vs Faroe Islands, 94th cap.

evidence.quote: His last match was on 20 November in the 1–1 draw against the Faroe Islands

events.text: Last game for Apollon Limassol before leaving the club.

evidence.quote: His last game was the 1–2 defeat against Nea Salamis played on 22 May

events.text: Signed with Chennaiyin in ISL; first Maltese player in India.

evidence.quote: On 27 August 2019 , Schembri signed a one-year contract with Indian Super League

events.label: retirement
events.text: Announced retirement from professional football.

evidence.quote: On 9 March 2020 , Schembri announced his retirement from professional football

events.text: Last professional match, ISL final vs ATK with Chennaiyin.

evidence.quote: with his last game being the ISL final against ATK on 14 March
